content.value_statement: JavaScript teams need repeatable tests that cover units, integrations, components, and user flows. This skill provides patterns for Jest, Vitest, Testing Library, mocking, fixtures, and TDD.
actual_capabilities: Explains Jest and Vitest configuration for TypeScript projects.
Shows unit tests for pure functions, services, async functions, and errors.
Demonstrates mocking for fetch, modules, dependency injection, and spies.
Covers integration, database, end-to-end, component, snapshot, and fixture tests.
Provides testing checklists and best practices for maintainable suites.
limitations: Examples are illustrative and require adaptation to each project.
Does not execute tests or inspect a repository without user-provided context.
Does not replace security, performance, or accessibility test design.
Assumes common JavaScript and TypeScript tooling.

use_cases.title: Add service unit tests
use_cases.description: Create tests for functions, classes, async services, error paths, and dependency boundaries.

use_cases.title: Test frontend components
use_cases.description: Plan component tests with Testing Library, semantic queries, user interactions, and snapshot boundaries.

use_cases.title: Standardize project testing
use_cases.description: Define framework setup, coverage expectations, fixtures, mocks, and CI-friendly test practices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a test setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic test setup for a TypeScript project using Vitest. Include configuration choices, folder layout, and first test examples.

prompt_templates.title: Design unit tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design unit tests for this JavaScript service. Cover successful results, validation errors, async failures, and mocked dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan integration tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan integration tests for this API workflow. Include setup, teardown, test data, authentication cases, and database cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Build a TDD strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TDD and CI testing strategy for this application. Include framework selection, test layers, fixtures, mocking rules, and coverage gates.

output_examples.input: Need tests for an async API service that fetches users.
output_examples.output: A test plan covering successful responses, not-found errors, mocked fetch calls, and assertions on returned user data.

output_examples.input: Need component tests for a user card.
output: Recommended Testing Library queries based on visible behavior.
Interaction cases for loading, success, empty, and error states.
Snapshot guidance limited to stable presentational output.

output_examples.output: A structured testing policy with unit, integration, fixture, mock, cleanup, and coverage recommendations.

best_practices: Start with behavior-focused tests before checking implementation details.
Mock external services and keep test data isolated from production data.
Use cleanup, fixtures, and clear assertions to prevent test pollution.
anti_patterns: Do not make tests depend on live third-party services by default.
Do not assert private implementation details when user behavior is available.
Do not share mutable fixtures across tests without resetting state.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Jest, Vitest, Testing Library, Supertest-style integration tests, and common JavaScript testing patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples and setup guidance include TypeScript-focused configurations and type-safe test practices.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing patterns and guidance. Test execution depends on the user environment and available tools.

faq.question: Can it help with mocking APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for mocking fetch, modules, injected dependencies, spies, and external services.

faq.question: Is it limited to backend code?
faq.answer: No. It includes frontend component tests, API tests, database tests, end-to-end tests, and snapshots.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Treat examples as templates, avoid real production credentials, and adapt every test to the project context.
